path_decisions.rationale: Trailing stop is the next exit mechanism in the priority chain; profit_target and trailing_stop interact — both must handle SHORT direction
Backtest engine has 1-bar slippage on exit timing + long-only assumption — these edge cases compound with profit_target and trailing_stop bugs
mean_reversion on_bar() is confirmed missing profit_target + max_holding — the most impactful gap for win rate; higher pheromone than entry_signal_strength

candidate_solution.summary: 12 specific bottlenecks in exit chain preventing 65%+ win rate, with exact fixes for profit_target direction handling, trailing stop SHORT support, mean_reversion on_bar() exit gaps, YAML wiring mismatches, and backtest engine direction handling

bottlenecks.title: profit_target_exit() is LONG-only — SHORT positions never hit profit target
bottlenecks.detail: Line 167: target_price = entry_price * (1.0 + profit_take_pct). Line 169: close >= target_price. For SHORT, target should be entry_price * (1.0 - profit_take_pct) and check should be close <= target_price. Currently SHORT trades only exit via max_holding_bars timeout at a loss.
bottlenecks.fix: Add direction parameter to profit_target_exit(). For LONG: target = entry*(1+pct), check close >= target. For SHORT: target = entry*(1-pct), check close <= target. The Signal model already carries Direction (models.py:67-72) but profit_target_exit never receives it.
bottlenecks.win_rate_impact: +8-15% — all SHORT trades currently lose by timeout instead of taking profit

bottlenecks.title: RSI-adaptive profit targets use global mean RSI across ALL entries, not per-entry RSI
bottlenecks.detail: rsi_at_entry = rsi[entries]; avg_entry_rsi = float(rsi_at_entry.mean()). With 100+ entries, this converges to ~50 (neutral), making the adaptive feature dead code. Line 263-266: only adjusts pct if avg > 70 or < 30, which rarely triggers with a global mean.
bottlenecks.fix: Compute per-entry RSI: for each entry at bar i, use rsi.iloc[i] as that entry's RSI. Then compute target = entry_price * (1 + adjusted_pct) where adjusted_pct depends on that specific entry's RSI. This requires restructuring profit_target_exit to accept per-entry adjustments or computing entry-specific targets before calling it.
bottlenecks.win_rate_impact: +3-5% — adaptive profit targets would lock in gains on overbought entries instead of waiting for reversal

bottlenecks.title: YAML take_profit_pct vs code profit_take_pct key mismatch — YAML values are dead letters
bottlenecks.detail: YAML sets take_profit_pct: 0.15 (trend), 0.05 (mean_rev), 0.10 (vol_breakout). Code reads profit_take_pct with defaults 0.10, 0.03, 0.05. The YAML keys never match the code param names so YAML values are never loaded. Same issue for stop_loss_pct and trailing_stop_atr_multiplier.
bottlenecks.fix: Align YAML key names with code param names: take_profit_pct → profit_take_pct, trailing_stop_atr_multiplier → trailing_stop_atr_mult, stop_loss_pct → stop_loss_pct (this one actually matches). Then load from YAML in __init__ via config system.
bottlenecks.win_rate_impact: +2-4% — YAML has better-calibrated values (0.15 for trend vs code default 0.10)

bottlenecks.title: Trailing stop tracks highest CLOSE not HIGH — premature exits on valid intra-bar pullbacks
bottlenecks.detail: highest.iloc[i] = max(float(close.iloc[i]), ...). Should use high.iloc[i] not close.iloc[i]. A bar where high=105, close=100 would set trailing to 100 instead of 105. Next bar close=98 would trigger exit even though the position was worth 105 at peak. This loses 5-7% of potential gain on winning trades.
bottlenecks.fix: Change highest tracking to use high values: highest.iloc[i] = max(float(high.iloc[i]), float(highest.iloc[i-1]) if i > 0 else float(high.iloc[i])). Requires high Series to be available in generate_signals (already available for both trend_following and volatility_breakout).
bottlenecks.win_rate_impact: +3-6% — prevents premature trailing stop exits on valid pullback bars

bottlenecks.title: Trailing stop is LONG-only — for SHORT positions should track lowest and check close > lowest + ATR*mult
bottlenecks.detail: trailing_exits = close < highest - trailing_atr * mult. For SHORT, the trailing stop should track the lowest price since entry and exit when close > lowest + ATR*mult. Currently SHORT positions have no trailing stop at all in generate_signals.
bottlenecks.fix: Track both highest_since_entry and lowest_since_entry. For LONG positions: exit when close < highest - ATR*mult. For SHORT positions: exit when close > lowest + ATR*mult. Requires direction information alongside entries (or separate long_entries/short_entries series).
bottlenecks.win_rate_impact: +5-10% — SHORT positions have no trailing stop protection at all

bottlenecks.title: YAML trailing_stop_atr_multiplier vs code trailing_stop_atr_mult — values diverge significantly
bottlenecks.detail: YAML sets trailing_stop_atr_multiplier: 1.5 (trend) and 2.0 (vol_breakout). Code defaults to 3.0 (trend) and 2.5 (vol_breakout). ATR*3.0 is far too wide — price must drop 3x ATR from peak before trailing fires, by which point most of the gain is lost.
bottlenecks.fix: Align YAML→code key names. Use YAML values (1.5 for trend, 2.0 for vol_breakout) as they are better calibrated. ATR*1.5 trailing is standard for trend-following systems.
bottlenecks.win_rate_impact: +4-7% — tighter trailing locks in more profit on winning trades

bottlenecks.title: BacktestEngine treats all non-LONG signals as SELL (closing long) — cannot simulate SHORT trades
bottlenecks.detail: side = OrderSide.BUY if signal.direction.value > 0 else OrderSide.SELL. For SHORT signals (direction.value = -1), this becomes SELL which reduces a long position instead of opening a short. The BacktestEngine (backtest.py:57-58) comment says 'long-only portfolio'. Win rate for SHORT-biased strategies is calculated as 0% because they never actually open.
bottlenecks.fix: In TradingSession._process_signal, check if a SHORT signal should open a short position: if no existing long position to close, submit SELL order to open short. In BacktestEngine, add short position tracking: entry_price when signal is SHORT, exit when opposite signal. Track separate PnL for short trades.
bottlenecks.win_rate_impact: +5-12% — mean_reversion and volatility_breakout SHORT entries currently produce zero wins

bottlenecks.title: BacktestEngine 1-bar exit timing slippage — exit signal at bar N, execution at bar N+1 open
bottlenecks.detail: for i in range(1,n): if entry_values[prev_idx]: entry_price = close_values[i]. When profit_target_exit fires at bar N (close >= target), BacktestEngine only sees exit_values[N] = True and executes at close[N+1]. If price gaps down between N close and N+1 open, the realized profit is lower than the profit_target threshold.
bottlenecks.fix: Add execution_price option: 'same_bar_close' (current behavior but using bar N close) vs 'next_bar_open' (current, bar N+1). For profit_target exits specifically, the target WAS hit at bar N so using bar N close is more realistic. Alternatively, use limit order simulation: if target was hit intra-bar, fill at target price.
bottlenecks.win_rate_impact: +2-3% — same-bar execution for profit_target exits captures the actual target profit instead of next-bar slippage

bottlenecks.title: mean_reversion on_bar() path has NO profit_target or max_holding check — trades can run indefinitely
bottlenecks.detail: The _latest_signal() method returns (Direction, bool) for entry and exit. The exit check (lines 107-109) only tests bb_upper*0.98 and bb_lower*0.98 conditions. There is no profit_target_exit integration, no max_holding_bars counter, and no trailing stop. In generate_signals() these are added (line 146-147), but the on_bar() event-driven path used in paper/live mode completely lacks them.
bottlenecks.fix: Add position tracking state to MeanReversionStrategy: entry_price, entry_direction, bars_since_entry. In on_bar(), after computing _latest_signal(), check: (1) profit_target: if in_position and entry_direction==LONG and close >= entry_price*(1+profit_take_pct) → emit FLAT; (2) SHORT profit_target: close <= entry_price*(1-profit_take_pct) → FLAT; (3) max_holding: bars_since_entry >= max_holding_bars → FLAT. This matches what generate_signals() does.
bottlenecks.win_rate_impact: +10-20% — mean_reversion in event-driven mode currently has ZERO profit-taking, making it the single biggest win rate gap

bottlenecks.title: mean_reversion generate_signals() merges long+short entries into single series, profit_target_exit treats all as LONG
bottlenecks.detail: entries = (long_count >= self._min_conditions) | (short_count >= self._min_conditions). This merges both directions into one boolean series. Then profit_target_exit(close, entries, pct, bars) assumes all entries are LONG (line 167: target = entry*(1+pct)). SHORT entries hit the wrong target direction and never profit-exit.
bottlenecks.fix: Split entries into long_entries and short_entries. Call profit_target_exit separately for each with appropriate direction. Or refactor profit_target_exit to accept a direction parameter alongside entries.
bottlenecks.win_rate_impact: +5-8% — mean_rev SHORT entries currently only exit via max_holding timeout

bottlenecks.title: mean_reversion volume_threshold default 0.8 is nearly always True — YAML says 1.2 which is meaningful
bottlenecks.detail: Code default: self._volume_threshold = p.get('volume_threshold', 0.8). This means volume > 0.8 * volume_ma, which is trivially satisfied (current volume > 80% of average). YAML sets volume_threshold: 1.2 (volume > 120% of average), a meaningful filter. With 0.8, the vol_ok condition is always True, making min_conditions=2 effectively = 1 of the 2 remaining conditions.
bottlenecks.fix: Change code default to 1.2 to match YAML, or load from YAML config. With proper volume filtering, fewer but higher-quality entries are taken, improving win rate.
bottlenecks.win_rate_impact: +2-4% — higher volume threshold filters out low-conviction entries

bottlenecks.title: signal_quality_metrics hit_rate uses 1-bar next-bar return as win proxy, not full trade lifecycle
bottlenecks.detail: forward_returns = close.pct_change().shift(-1) uses only the next bar's return. A signal that leads to a 5-bar trade with +15% profit but next-bar -1% return would be counted as a miss. This overestimates bad signals and underestimates good signals, distorting validation.
bottlenecks.fix: Add trade_lifecycle_hit_rate: simulate entries/exits through BacktestEngine and measure actual trade win rate. Keep 1-bar hit_rate as a fast proxy but add lifecycle-based metric for GO/NO-GO decisions.
bottlenecks.win_rate_impact: +1-2% — better validation prevents filtering out good signals that have negative next-bar returns

priority_order.reason: mean_rev on_bar() has ZERO profit taking — single biggest gap, +10-20% win rate
profit_target_exit LONG-only — all SHORT trades lose, +8-15% win rate
BacktestEngine cannot simulate SHORT — SHORT wins invisible, +5-12%
Trailing stop LONG-only — no SHORT trailing protection, +5-10%
mean_rev merged entries — SHORT entries hit wrong target, +5-8%
Trailing stop ATR mult too wide in code vs YAML, +4-7%
Trailing tracks CLOSE not HIGH — premature exits, +3-6%
RSI-adaptive uses global mean — dead code, +3-5%
YAML→code key mismatch — better values unused, +2-4%

exit_priority_chain_analysis.description: When multiple exit conditions are simultaneously True, which fires first?
exit_priority_chain_analysis.current_behavior: exits = exits | profit_exits | trailing_exits — all OR'd together, no priority. The BacktestEngine processes the first True exit it encounters in bar order.
exit_priority_chain_analysis.problem: If profit_target fires on the same bar as a trailing_stop or technical_exit, the actual fill depends on which condition the engine sees first. Since profit_target is the most desirable exit (guaranteed profit), it should take priority.
exit_priority_chain_analysis.fix: Implement priority-ordered exit chain: 1) profit_target (highest priority — guaranteed gain), 2) trailing_stop (locks in most profit), 3) max_holding_timeout (time-based stop), 4) technical_exit (lowest — may give back gains). When multiple are True on same bar, profit_target wins.

notes: Estimated combined win rate impact if all 12 bottlenecks fixed: +30-55% on top of current baseline. The two most impactful fixes are (1) adding profit_target+max_holding to mean_reversion on_bar() path and (2) making profit_target_exit direction-aware. Both affect every SHORT trade and every mean_reversion live trade. The YAML→code key mismatch is a systemic issue affecting all 3 strategies — once fixed, the YAML-calibrated values automatically improve defaults. The exit priority chain (profit_target > trailing_stop > max_holding > technical_exit) should be implemented as an ordered evaluation, not a simple OR.
